page.layout: Printed page with one text block. Top right: page number. Above the title: a woodcut headpiece. Then a centred title (level 1 head) with a subtitle. Below it: a single column of verse in stanzas, with a woodcut initial Q opening the first stanza. No margin notes, no running head, no catchword or signature.

main_text.head: CANTICUM SYMEONIS ex secundo capite Euangelij secundum Lucam.

p.i: QUum te puellum, Christe, senilibus Excepit ulnis debilior Symon, Clarus propinqua morte vates Tale pio dedit ore carmen.
NUNC laeta venit, summe Parens, dies: Nunc me solutum corpore liberans Promissa præstas, seruulumque Pace tuum potiore donas.
Sperata priscis nam tua patribus Nunc missa caelo conspicitur salus Gaudente: præsentemq; nostris Illam oculis licet intueri.
Illam statuto tempore Gentibus Cunctis fruendam nunc, Pater, obiicis: Quacunque sol feruens iacentes Purpureo fouet igne terras.
Qua caeca fictis religionibus Nox ante plebes implicuit vagas, Iam pulsa vanescet: per orbem Luce tua radiante totum.

page.notes: The large initial Q is a woodcut and is joined to the first word (QUum). The small-capital opening words are rendered as capitals (QUUM, NUNC) with u for the vowel. The faint mirrored text at the lower left is show-through and is left out. The last stanza line runs on to the next page, so it is not marked as continued. Letters: long s is written as plain s, and the ligature æ is kept as printed in præstas and præsentemq;. Possible spelling variants: "solutum" and "seruulumque" are read from a small, slightly blurred print.
